records.name: People's Music Supply
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit built around collective improvised music. It runs open improvisation labs, a concert series and monthly events, and it hosts members' shows at local venues.
records.what_you_do: Musicians can join the open improvisation labs, held on Tuesday evenings. Listeners can attend the concerts and events, which each link to a registration page.

schedule.text: Open Improvisation Labs on Tuesday evenings at 7 pm, and World to Come concerts on Wednesdays at 5:30 pm, running through October and November 2026. Other events run to December 2026.

cost.text: Not listed on the events page

first_step.how: Register for the Open Improvisation Lab at The Living Signal on Tuesday, Oct 13 at 7 pm, using the More info link on the group's events page
first_step.basis: Events are posted publicly with registration links, but the page does not say whether the labs suit beginners

records.notes: Legal name Peoples Music Supply Inc (IRS list). Homepage describes the group as a Philadelphia-based 501(c)(3). Venues named on the events page: Christ Church Gardens, The Living Signal, Molly's Books and Records, Egner Memorial Chapel, Upstairs Abyssinia, Lerner Center, and Point Breeze (address by email). Some listed events are run by members rather than the group. Street addresses and prices are not published. An email address on one event page belongs to that event and is not recorded as the group's contact. Newest dated item: a December 11, 2026 event.

records.name: Philadelphia Justice Project for Women & Girls
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that works to stop punishing women and girls who are survivors of gender violence. It gives legal help, pushes for policy change, trains court and police staff, and takes on volunteers and interns.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers bring skills such as legal help, research, counseling, teaching, photography and fundraising. Interns do research and writing, outreach, advocacy campaigns, and parole and commutation paperwork.

first_step.how: Email info@phillyjusticeproject.org to talk about which volunteer role fits your skills and schedule
first_step.basis: Anyone can contact the group about volunteering; internships are limited to students and no openings were posted

records.notes: Legal name Philadelphia Justice Project for Women & Girls (IRS list). No dated events or news on the site; the 2026 footer is not evidence. The Villanova undergraduate chapter ran from 2020 to 2025 and is past. Internships are unpaid and hybrid, with in-person meetings, court hearings and prison or jail trips, and are open to law students, graduate students in the social sciences and advanced undergraduates. Status is probably_active because the site works but shows no dates. Open_to is public for volunteering; internships are student-only.

records.name: Southeast Youth Athletic Association (SEYAA)
records.summary: A volunteer-run youth sports league in South Philadelphia. More than 1,000 kids play baseball, soccer and flag football on its five fields at Seventh and Bigler, all year round.
records.what_you_do: Kids join a baseball, soccer or flag football program. Volunteers run the leagues and prepare the fields, and the leagues raise money to cover utilities, insurance and liability costs.

schedule.text: Baseball, soccer and flag football are played year round on the league fields. Volunteers prepare the fields for summer soccer after the baseball playoffs.

locations.label: League fields
locations.address: Seventh and Bigler streets, South Philadelphia

first_step.how: Visit the fields at Seventh and Bigler during a game and ask a volunteer how to sign a child up for the next baseball, soccer or flag football season
first_step.basis: Open to area kids, but the sign-up steps were not published in the sources we read

records.notes: Legal name Southeast Youth Athletic Association Inc (IRS list). No group website was found in one search. The Inquirer article is dated May 30, 2026 and reports that the planned I-76 ramp no longer crosses the league's fields. A ProPublica search result for a SEYAA carries EIN 46-3404583, which is not the IRS EIN in our list (23-2747538), so it was not used. The IRS list address, 1133 Durfor St (19148), is not confirmed as a field or office address. Cost and sign-up steps were not found.

records.name: Stray Cat Relief Fund
records.summary: A nonprofit that cares for stray and feral cats in the Philadelphia and New Jersey area. Volunteers trap, neuter, vaccinate and return colony cats, and foster homes and a small adoption space help rescued cats find homes.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers help trap, transport and care for cats and colonies. Foster families care for cats until they are adopted, and the group lends humane traps.

first_step.how: Email purr@straycatrelieffund.org to ask about volunteering, or fill out the foster application linked on the homepage
first_step.basis: Volunteering and fostering are open to anyone who asks, and the site lists no requirements

records.notes: Legal name Stray Cat Relief Fund (IRS list). The IRS list spells the website straycatreliefund.org, which does not resolve; the group's own site and email use straycatrelieffund.org, which was used instead. The newest dated item on the site is 'In 2024' (year-only annual totals), so status is unknown rather than guessed. The footer year 2023 is not used. Mailing address on the group's site: PO Box 20167, Philadelphia 19145. A third-party listing gives a different PO box (54845, 19148), not recorded. A 2017 news story names the group as a fundraising organizer; too old to count. The volunteer page is linked but its text was not shown. Donations go through PayPal and Venmo.

records.name: Pennsylvania Association of Naturopathic Physicians
records.summary: A statewide membership group for naturopathic doctors in Pennsylvania. It shares news about state registration and lists educational events for practitioners.
records.what_you_do: The group offers membership at several levels, with benefits listed on its membership pages. The site also has a directory for finding a naturopathic doctor.

first_step.how: Open the Become a Member page on the website to read the membership levels and dues
first_step.basis: Joining requires dues, and the membership page itself was not read in full

records.notes: Legal name The Pennsylvania Association of Naturopathic Physicians Inc. Statewide group based in Harrisburg, not a Philadelphia group; included with low confidence for the owner to decide, and the owner may prefer to hide it as a trade association. The newest dated item is a news note on state registration as of March 20, 2024. The educational events page lists a 2023 virtual conference (past) and an undated herb symposium with no date or venue. The events listing on the separate events page did not load. The Atlantic Naturopathic Conference and the Medicines from the Earth symposium are events, not groups, so they were not followed.

records.name: W.O.R.X. (Works of Raphael Xavier)
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings arts training to young people from underserved African American communities, with a focus on Breaking, a dance form from hip hop culture. It runs youth programs, often with local schools, and hosts community jams and festivals.
records.what_you_do: Youth take part in arts programs, often through local schools. Community members can come to the annual Core Creek jam to ride, dance and play games.

schedule.text: Youth programming runs through the year, with no weekly times on the page. Community jams are one-off events.

cost.text: The 2026 jam was free or donation based. No other costs are listed.

first_step.how: Come to the next community jam, or use the contact page to ask about youth programs
first_step.basis: The jam is open to families and newcomers, but youth program enrollment is not described

records.notes: Legal name W O R X Works of Raphael Xavier Inc (IRS list). Borderline for the owner: the only 2026 event is at Core Creek Park in Langhorne, Bucks County, and no Philadelphia youth program is named. Other dated items on the page are 2016 to 2020, including Philadelphia events in 2016 and 2017 (City Hall, Kimmel Center) and an online event in 2020. The page says the youth programs run in and out of Pennsylvania. Youth programs are aimed at underserved African American youth, so open_to is public for the events only. The Institute for Cultural Partnerships is named on the page as a related body; it has no link there and was not checked.

records.name: Women Matter Alliance
records.summary: A group that supports domestic violence survivors with legal advocacy, social and mental health help, and job coaching. It serves survivors of all genders, including LGBTQ+ survivors, and it welcomes volunteers with skills such as legal advice and social media.
records.what_you_do: Survivors can ask about the group's legal advocacy, social and mental health services, and job coaching. Volunteers bring skills such as legal advice, social media, accounting, or help recruiting advisors and board members.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the website to ask about services, or about volunteering with your skills
first_step.basis: The site lists no intake steps, service hours or eligibility, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: Legal name Women Matter Alliance (IRS list). The site does not name a Philadelphia office or service area; the IRS list address, 1321 S Opal St (19146), is the only Philadelphia link found. The phone number on the site, 1.800.799.7233, appears to be the national domestic violence hotline and is not recorded as this group's phone. A second listed number with a 609 area code is also not recorded. No dated events or news. Status is probably_active because the site works but shows no dates. Owner may want to confirm the service area before publishing.

records.name: Unitas Ensemble
records.summary: An orchestra based in Boston that plays Latin American music. Its website describes concerts and school outreach in the Boston area.
records.notes: The IRS list gives 1539 S Cleveland St, Philadelphia 19146, but the website describes a Boston orchestra with Boston venues and press. Not checked whether the Philadelphia filer is the same entity; this may be a name collision. The 2018 copyright footer is not used. No dated events on the site. Owner may want a second search for the Philadelphia filer before this is final.

records.name: University Surplus Property Association
records.summary: A national membership association for university and college surplus property programs. It offers member training, policy templates and a yearly conference.
records.notes: No Philadelphia office, meeting or program appears on the site. Membership is for institutions, with a $100 individual higher education membership. The next conference is listed for March 2027 in Kentucky. The public is pointed to a member map for surplus items, not to a group the public joins. Not a Philadelphia community group.

notes: Batch w20a-17: 15 groups in the input. Verdicts: 13 publish (7 with dated evidence or a working page, 6 unknown and held back), 2 out_of_area. Searches: 2 of 2 used (SEYAA and Stray Cat Relief Fund); the cap is reached, so Philly Solidarity, Resident Action Committee II, Soul Food CDC, Succor Inc and Vitamin D Productions got no search and stay unknown. Fetches: 21 of 60; the fetch budget was not reached. Borderline calls for the owner: W.O.R.X. (only 2026 event is in Bucks County), Pennsylvania Association of Naturopathic Physicians (statewide trade association, dormant), Women Matter Alliance (no Philadelphia link on its site), and Unitas Ensemble (Boston orchestra with a Philadelphia IRS address, possibly a name collision). IRS list problems: the Stray Cat Relief Fund website is misspelled; the Philly Solidarity website does not resolve; Soul Food, Resident Action Committee II, Succor and Vitamin D list text or a zip code instead of a web address; the South Philly Boxing Gym site returned empty text. The Institute for Cultural Partnerships is named on the W.O.R.X. page and was not checked (no link). The unknown records have no summary, category or source because nothing was read, so the publish rules hold them back.
